evidence.excerpt: Internet of Things deployments in industrial and smart city environments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous network traffic across geographically distributed edge nodes. Centralising this data for intrusion detection raises significant privacy and bandwidth concerns, particularly in multi-stakeholder environments. This paper proposes a federated learning framework for distributed intrusion detection, wherein each edge node trains a local anomaly detection model on its own traffic and periodically shares only model gradient updates with a central aggregation server. The aggregated global model is then redistributed to participating nodes, enabling collective knowledge improvement without raw data exposure. The framework is evaluated on a purpose-built IoT testbed consisting of twenty-four heterogeneous edge devices simulating smart metering, environmental sensing, and industrial actuation scenarios. Results demonstrate that the federated approach achieves detection accuracy within 3% of a centralised baseline while reducing data transmission overhead by over 80%. The paper also investigates the robustness of the framework against poisoning attacks introduced by compromised edge nodes.
